title: Does an epipolar gate help bundle adjustment under the mismatch mix a real SIFT matcher produces?
lede: feeding sensing-matchreal's measured SIFT mismatch mixes into the sensing-epigate trial, gate plus Cauchy beats a RANSAC start at ratio tests of 0.8 and tighter (0.0078 against 0.0207 object radii at 0.8) and loses only at a loose 0.9 ratio test, where all methods exceed 0.08; synthetic geometry, 6 seeds
summary: sensing-epigate found a fundamental-matrix gate no better than a RANSAC start against invented mismatches; sensing-matchreal then measured real SIFT mismatches on a Middlebury stereo pair. This project runs the epigate trial with each measured mix (rate and along/near/far shares at ratio tests none, 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6). Gate plus Cauchy adjustment gives 0.0078, 0.0033 and 0.0026 object radii at ratio 0.8, 0.7 and 0.6, against 0.0207, 0.0058 and 0.0032 for a RANSAC start and 0.43, 0.013 and 0.0057 for plain Cauchy (floor 0.0015). At ratio 0.9 (23% wrong) the RANSAC start is better (0.082 against 0.130) and with no ratio test (56% wrong) nothing works. An all-uniform control at the same rates is dominated by single failed seeds and is reported as unestablished. Limits: one scene and detector for the mix, synthetic orbit geometry, independent draws, 6 seeds, no intervals, untuned gate.
